note: Every number the garment solver takes from outside, what it supports and how solid it is. 'measured' means an instrument measurement on a named fabric; 'bracket' means a stated range with a chosen central value where no measurement was found in the time allowed.

silk_chiffon.status: measured pair (one fabric, one laboratory, weft direction only)
silk_chiffon.basis: Fabric weight 0.256 N/m2 (ASTM D3776) and flexural rigidity G_P = 0.502 uN m from a modified ASTM D1388 cantilever (Shirley tester, 42.9 deg, strips 152 x 25 mm cut along the weft); a Griesser-Taylor fit gave 0.527 uN m.
silk_chiffon.citation: Fuss F.K. (2024) Drag measurements of fluttering fabrics and their application for sportswear. Sports Engineering 27:38, Table 1. doi:10.1007/s12283-024-00477-1
silk_chiffon.bracket: Common chiffon is 6-8 momme, 0.026-0.035 kg/m2 (the lead's bracket 0.03-0.04 kg/m2); B scales with weight roughly as weight^2 to weight^3, so a heavier chiffon is stiffer.
silk_chiffon.supports: skirt fabric in the delivered sequences; terminal speed and bending-length validation

silk_georgette.status: measured pair (one fabric, one laboratory, weft direction only)
silk_georgette.basis: Fabric weight 0.336 N/m2 and G_P = 0.602 uN m (Griesser-Taylor 0.681 uN m), same method as the chiffon.
silk_georgette.citation: Fuss F.K. (2024), Sports Engineering 27:38, Table 1. doi:10.1007/s12283-024-00477-1
silk_georgette.bracket: Georgette ranges 8-14 momme, 0.034-0.06 kg/m2 (the lead's bracket 0.05-0.06 kg/m2 is a heavier georgette).
silk_georgette.supports: water-sleeve fabric in the delivered sequences (modern dance sleeves are sold as chiffon and are properly georgette, see water_sleeves)

silk_crepe_de_chine.basis: Areal density bracket 0.06-0.07 kg/m2 (12-16 momme). Bending rigidity bracket 1-3 uN m (bending length 1.2-1.7 cm on Earth), central 1.5 uN m chosen. The nearest measured fabric, a 'crepe lavable' of unstated fibre at 0.0368 kg/m2, had G_P = 0.581 uN m (Fuss 2024, Table 1).
silk_crepe_de_chine.citation: KES-F data for silk crepe de chine exist in Matsudaira M. & Kawabata S. (1988) A study of the mechanical properties of woven silk fabrics, Part I, J. Text. Inst. 79(3):458-475, doi:10.1080/00405008808658280 (paywalled, not read).

silk_satin_heavy.basis: Areal density bracket 0.08-0.10 kg/m2 (19-23 momme charmeuse to a light duchess satin). Bending rigidity bracket 2-6 uN m, central 3 uN m chosen (bending length 1.5 cm on Earth). No woven-satin KES-F or cantilever value was found; the knit 'charmeuse' fabrics in Fuss (2024) are warp knits and were not used.
silk_satin_heavy.citation: none measured; Matsudaira & Kawabata (1988) as above for silk weaves generally

shear_stiffness.value: 0.3-0.5 gf/cm/deg (16.9-28.1 N/m per radian) by fabric
shear_stiffness.basis: Usual KES-F shear rigidity G of light silk weaves, about 0.2-0.6 gf/cm/deg; no value read from a primary source in this work.
shear_stiffness.supports: in-plane shear (bias) compliance; it has little effect at these loads

tensile_stiffness.basis: KES-F extensibility EM of 3-10% at 490 N/m gives secant stiffness 5000-16000 N/m; at the loads met here (below 1 N/m) any value in that range keeps strains below 1e-3, and the one-pass solver is stiffer than this in practice.

c_normal.basis: Drag coefficient of a thin flat plate normal to the flow, disc and square plate about 1.17-1.18 at Re above 1e4; it rises toward 2 for long plates. Aspect ratio changes it little up to 10.
c_normal.citation: Hoerner S.F. (1965) Fluid-Dynamic Drag, ch. 3; Fail R., Lawford J.A. & Eyre R.C.W. (1957) Low-speed experiments on the wake characteristics of flat plates normal to an air stream, ARC R&M 3120 (abstract seen).
c_normal.supports: normal pressure on every triangle, -1/2 rho C_N |v_n| v_n A; it also carries the lift of inclined panels (as C_N sin^2 of incidence)

c_tangent.status: textbook formula applied to the case
c_tangent.basis: Both faces together, on the one-sided area: 2 x 1.328 / sqrt(Re_L) for a laminar plate is 0.008-0.027 for Re_L = 1e4-1e5 (garment panels 0.1-1 m at 0.2-3 m/s; nu = 1.3e-5 m2/s on the Moon, 1.5e-5 on Earth).
c_tangent.citation: Blasius laminar skin friction, e.g. Schlichting H. & Gersten K., Boundary-Layer Theory.
c_tangent.supports: skin friction along every triangle, -1/2 rho C_T |v_t| v_t A

flag_drag_context.basis: Flexible sheets aligned with the flow carry time-averaged drag coefficients from about 0.02 to 2 depending on flutter; the solver resolves flutter itself, so only skin friction is added along the surface.
flag_drag_context.citation: Carruthers A.C. & Filippone A. (2005) Aerodynamic drag of streamers and flags, J. Aircraft 42(4):976-982; Raynaud & Mulleners (2026) arXiv:2602.06237; Fuss (2024).

air_density.basis: Moon: sea-level datum of the project's climate, climate/results/gcm/global_winds_A28_dim5_moon.json at height 0 km (common.md); Earth: ISA sea level.

permeability.basis: Air bleeding through an open chiffon weave is neglected: at dynamic pressures of about 1 Pa the Darcy through-flow of light silks is of order 1% of the panel speed (air permeability of order 10^2-10^3 L/m2/s at 100 Pa, scaled linearly). Not checked against a measured chiffon value here.

friction.basis: KES-SE mean friction MIU of spun-silk fabric 0.141 against a steel-wire contactor; forearm skin 0.42 +/- 0.19 against the same contactor; skin against fabric 0.2-0.35 at 25% skin moisture and 0.55-0.65 at 52%.
friction.citation: Inoue M. (2011) Surface friction properties of fabrics and human skin. In Ghrib T. (ed.) New Tribological Ways, InTech, pp. 265-272.
friction.supports: Coulomb friction of cloth on the body's capsules and on the floor (the floor value has no source)

water_sleeves.status: popular and commercial sources; choice inside the brief's 1.2-2.0 m
water_sleeves.basis: Opera water sleeves: men's about 1 chi (33 cm), women's about 2 chi (67 cm), at most 3 chi; in particular plays and since the 1970s dan sleeves of 6-8 chi (2.0-2.7 m) or more. Classical-dance sleeves are sold at 1.2, 1.5, 2 and 3 m, about 1.5 m recommended, panel width 72 cm; fabric originally silk, now mostly sold as chiffon and properly georgette. The circumference 0.50 m (a loose cuff) is a modelling choice between a fitted cuff (0.3 m) and the 0.72 m panel.
water_sleeves.citation: NetEase, '戏曲知识之水袖' (2019-02-21), https://www.163.com/dy/article/E8HL4K7L053734RJ.html; Baidu Baike '水袖功' and a ximalaya Q&A page (seen only as search summaries).

circle_skirt.waist: 2 cm above the omphalion, band radius 6 mm outside the abdomen capsule
circle_skirt.basis: Natural waist just above the navel; skirt length leaves the hem 17 cm above the floor standing (mid-calf to above the ankle).

cross_check: The dance literature helper's record (/media/projectspace/terluna-research/humanities/agents/literature/sources.json, entries fuss2024, morris_thomas_steen2009, water_sleeves_encyclopaedia) reads the same Fuss (2024) Table 1 values; it lists KES-F bending and shear of silk crepe de chine, habotai and satin, flag drag coefficients and the air permeability of chiffon as open. Fuss (2024) also measured mean drag coefficients of 0.87-1.07 for ten fluttering fabric strips on a cylinder (Re 6e4-2.8e5), context for C_N near 1.

Macklin M., Storey K., Lu M., Terdiman P., Chentanez N., Jeschke S. & Mueller M. (2019) Small steps in physics simulation. SCA.
Mueller M., Chentanez N., Kim T.-Y. & Macklin M. (2014) Strain based dynamics. SCA.
Bergou M., Wardetzky M., Harmon D., Zorin D. & Grinspun E. (2006) A quadratic bending model for inextensible surfaces. SGP.
Wardetzky M., Bergou M., Harmon D., Zorin D. & Grinspun E. (2007) Discrete quadratic curvature energies. CAGD 24.
Meyer M., Desbrun M., Schroeder P. & Barr A. (2003) Discrete differential-geometry operators for triangulated 2-manifolds.
Peirce F.T. (1930) The handle of cloth as a measurable quantity. J. Text. Inst. 21:T377-T416 (bending length c = (B/w)^(1/3); 41.5 deg cantilever).
